title: whiteboard writes are absent from event_log, so nothing can say who wrote a board row, when, or with which arguments
body:
Whiteboard writes are absent from `event_log`. On devbin's store it held 298 rows across 25 distinct ops -- `issues.*`, `ac.*`, `at.*`, `st.*`, `wp.*`, `attachment.put`, `disk.*` -- and not one whiteboard op. The control is positive: the log's only row after 06:00Z on 2026-09-16 is a `disk.sync_to_disk` at 07:02:41.791Z, and whiteboard writes at known times fall on both sides of it (registrations at 06:30:43Z, 06:45:39Z and 06:59:44Z; pickups at 06:32:21Z and 06:47:09Z; three migrates at 07:01:28Z; adds, an archive and a pickup at 08:57:03Z and 09:00:52Z), none recorded. The item and node times come from the rows' own `recorded_at`, `migrated_at` and `archived_at`. Devbin letter J, measured by both.

Found by devbin migrating its boards on Intent 3.0.3 (`d24487079`), sent through intent/vc on hv's routing, and ruled by hv on 2026-09-16 to be fixed in this release (hv decision 18). The full measurement record, with the instrument (`carry-map.sh`, driven red and green) and who measured what, is devbin `1824c75`, `intent/whiteboard/dc/.history/20260916/wb-upstream-defects-draft.md`.

Consequence: the store can say what a board row holds but not who wrote it, from which session, or with which arguments -- which is why the foreign registration in the `wb register` issue filed with this one cannot be attributed. With the `updated_at` issue (devbin letter O) the store keeps no trace that a board row was ever edited after insert.

Fix: every whiteboard write records an event, with the acting node and the verb's arguments, through the same door the other ops use.

**CLOSED 2026-09-16, landed on vc's word with bank 1 (0411, 0415, 0414) under vc decisions 21 (2) and 22.** Every whiteboard verb now records one `wb.*` event naming the acting node and the verb's arguments, in the same transaction as the rows it writes: the board writers moved off `Store` onto `WbWrite`, which a verb gets only from `Store::wb_write` with its envelope in hand. The ops are rostered in `KNOWN_OPS`, `wb touch` included. A verb that moves no row commits nothing and records nothing. A restore (`sync --to-store`) records no board event, because its act is the sync, which the sync records. Guarded by `tests/wb_writes_are_recorded.rs`.
